Hi HG,

Nice to have you back. I want to play devil's advocate part for this post. I believe lots of things can be learned from those situations which your plan basically "did not work". Lets look at this EURUSD H1 chart as an example.

I believe the climber I marked is a valid climber and with bars 1,2 and 3 its buying zone is confirmed. After confirmation we wait for price to give us a signal inside the zone. And price comes back to zone and we have nice engulfing bar #5 over hammer-like bar #4. If I had traded live I would probably buy it after the close of bar #5. Maybe I would wait a bit better(lower) price then the close of bar#5. But still I would go for it. And then Iook what happens. It just falls back.

It even invalidates the zone. So here are my questions:

1. Would you also buy this? If not what would be your reasoning not to buy it? 2. Where would you put your stopLoss. Or do you cancel the trade if you think it will not move in your favor. But what would be your trigger for this?

Thanks in advance.

Again nice to hear from you.

Akif,

akifusenet wrote: Hi HG,..Nice to have you back.... I believe the climber I marked is a valid climber and with bars 1,2 and 3 its buying zone is confirmed. After confirmation we wait for price to give us a signal inside the zone. And price comes back to zone and we have nice engulfing bar #5 over hammer-like bar #4. If I had traded live I would probably buy it after the close of bar #5. Maybe I would wait a bit better(lower) price then the close of bar#5. But still I would go for it. And then Iook what happens. It just falls back. It even invalidates the zone. So here are my questions:

1. Would you also buy this? If not what would be your reasoning not to buy it? 2. Where would you put your stopLoss. Or do you cancel the trade if you think it will not move in your favor. But what would be your trigger for this?

Thanks in advance.

Again nice to hear from you.

Akif,

Thanks for the kind words.

First I would start out by saying losses happen in trading. They are the cost of doing business. In fact, some call trading a loser's game. Where he who loses best, wins.

Personally, I do not see that as an engulfing pattern. Based on the chart, it looks like the body of candle #5 does not fully engulf the body of candle #4. It looks like the open is equal to the close. So it's not engulfing. In such a case, I would at least like to see the range of candle # 5 engulfing the range of candle #4 and the close of #5 greater than the high of #4. So #5 would have to be an OUTSIDE bar.

There is an entry signal that I have been flirting with that appears hear. It is not perfect, but let's assume it is for discussion. The entry signal is the "confirmation entry" signal. You can find information on it at YouTube or on the PIE II thread at FF.

From this point on unless otherwise stated, when I refer to a number it will be the numbers in black which I have labeled.

#1 is our "stop run candle". I don't like the fact that the upper wick is equal in size to the body of this candle. If the upper wick was bigger than the body, then I would not consider this our start point or "stop run candle".

#2 meets the requirements for the "confirmation interval". It closes higher than the body of the previous candle and it closes in the upper 66 percentile of the range.

At this point, we have a maximum of 3 intervals for price to retrace back into the wick of our "stop run candle". The idea being, that we want to place a stop a few pips below the low of the "stop run candle". Therefore, we would like to minimize our risk by entering as low as possible. One can choose to wait for a 50% retracement of that lower wick to enter. In this case that did not happen. But let's assume a more aggressive style. So we are simply waiting for a retrace that is lower than the low of candle #2 and back into the lower wick of candle #1.

We get this at #4. Now we are in the market. Our risk is defined as the shaded area.

Ultimately, we take a loss on this trade. But take a look at the yellow arrow. The arrow points to a down WRB that closes lower then the low of the candle that triggered us into the market. This could have served as an early warning that the trade was not going to work. So an early exit could be contemplated at this time. One key here is that the WRB occurs within 1-5 intervals after the trigger bar.

ممنون از کلمات مهربانانه‌ات.

اول باید بگویم ضررها در معامله اتفاق می‌افتند؛ آن‌ها هزینهٔ انجام کارند. در واقع بعضی‌ها معامله را بازی بازنده‌ها می‌نامند، جایی که کسی که بهتر بازنده شود، می‌برد.

شخصاً من آن را یک الگوی اینگالف نمی‌بینم. بر اساس چارت، به نظر می‌رسد بدنهٔ کندل #5 بدنهٔ کندل #4 را کاملاً اینگالف نمی‌کند؛ به نظر می‌رسد open برابر close است، پس اینگالف نیست. در چنین حالتی حداقل دوست دارم رنج کندل #5 رنج کندل #4 را اینگالف کند و closeِ #5 از سقف #4 بزرگ‌تر باشد؛ یعنی #5 باید یک OUTSIDE bar باشد.

یک سیگنال ورود هست که مدتی است با آن سر و کار دارم و اینجا ظاهر می‌شود. کامل نیست، اما برای بحث فرض می‌کنیم کامل است. آن سیگنال ورود، سیگنال «confirmation entry» است. می‌توانی اطلاعاتش را در YouTube یا در ترد PIE II در FF پیدا کنی.

از این به بعد، مگر اینکه خلافش گفته شود، وقتی به عددی اشاره می‌کنم منظورم اعداد مشکی است که لیبل زده‌ام.

#1 «stop run candle» ماست. دوست ندارم فیتی بالایی این کندل دقیقاً برابر بدنهٔ آن باشد؛ اگر فیتی بالایی از بدنه بزرگ‌تر بود، این را نقطهٔ شروع یا «stop run candle» خودمان در نظر نمی‌گرفتم.

#2 شرایط «confirmation interval» را برآورده می‌کند؛ بالاتر از بدنهٔ کندل قبلی می‌بندد و در 66 درصد بالایی رنج بسته می‌شود.

در این نقطه، حداکثر 3 بازه برای قیمت داریم تا به فیتی «stop run candle» خودمان برگردد. ایده این است که می‌خواهیم استاپ را چند پیپ زیر کف «stop run candle» بگذاریم؛ پس می‌خواهیم با ورود در پایین‌ترین حالت ممکن ریسک را کمینه کنیم. می‌توانی صبر کنی تا 50% بازگشت آن فیتی پایینی برای ورود؛ در این مورد این اتفاق نیفتاد. اما بیایم سبک تهاجمی‌تری فرض کنیم؛ پس فقط منتظر بازگشتی می‌مانیم که پایین‌تر از کف کندل #2 باشد و به فیتی پایینی کندل #1 برگردد.

این را در #4 می‌گیریم؛ حالا داخل بازاریم. ریسک ما به‌صورت ناحیهٔ سایه‌دار تعریف می‌شود.

در نهایت در این معامله ضرر می‌کنیم. اما به فلش زرد نگاه کن؛ فلش به یک WRB نزولی اشاره می‌کند که پایین‌تر از کف کندلی که ما را به بازار کشانده می‌بندد. این می‌توانست هشدار زودهنگام باشد که معامله جواب نخواهد داد، پس در این زمان می‌توانست خروج زودهنگام در نظر گرفته شود. یک نکتهٔ کلیدی اینجاست که WRB ظرف 1-5 بازه بعد از بار تریگر رخ می‌دهد.

hieronymus wrote: This is DTFL confirming entry, modified for lower TF and incorporating WRB/S&D....

Please, post as much as you want.

The entry definitely needs to be "modified" for our purposes. The first modification for me is that an entry signal is "valid" as long as at least one tick/pip of the pattern is in or one a Buying or Selling Aggression Zone. Another modification is that the "Stop run" candle should: (1) make a higher high (for shorts) or a lower low (for longs) than the previous interval. (2) The Upper/lower shadow of the "Stop run" candle should be larger than the combination of the body and the opposite shadow. (3) The initial "Stop run" candle needs to appear 1-3 intervals after a WRB.

Another modification under review has to do with the confirmation candle. While it still needs to close below the body of the previous candle (for shorts), instead of having to close in its lower 33%, it only has to have a larger body than the previous interval.

The pictures in the previous post do not meet some of these modifications. However, I am pretty sure that these mods (along with some others) will eventually create the actual confirmation entry signal used.

This picture does meet the modifications so far discussed. Except that it did not appear on or near a Zone so no trade would have been taken.

More examples with the modifications.

The rules:

1. There may be a variation that does not include a WRB, but as of this time the first requirement is the appearance of a WRB

2. After the appearance of a WRB, we need to see the "Stop run" candle(#1) within 1-3 intervals. Rather than thinking of this interval as a "Stop run" candle, it may be more appropriate to think of it as Supply Swamping Demand (SSD) for shorts or Demand Swamping Supply (DSS) for longs. In the case of SSD, the candle's upper shadow must be greater than the combination of the body and the lower shadow. The SSD candle must also make a higher high than the previous candle.

3. The confirmation candle must close lower than the body of the previous candle (for shorts) and higher than the body of the previous candle for longs. The other requirement is that the body of the confirmation candle is larger than the body of the previous candle.

4. After the confirmation candle (#2), price must retrace to within the range of the upper shadow (for short) within 3 intervals. Excluding the WRB, this is a minimum 3 interval pattern and a maximum 5 interval pattern.

That's what we have so far............

The first modification for me is that an entry signal is "valid" as long as at least one tick/pip of the pattern is in or one a Buying or Selling Aggression Zone.

Most definitely, they have an arbitrary number just to have a rule. Many of their rules are like that actually. Price entering or hitting a zone is enough.

Another modification is that the "Stop run" candle should: (1) make a higher high (for shorts) or a lower low (for longs) than the previous interval. (2) The Upper/lower shadow of the "Stop run" candle should be larger than the combination of the body and the opposite shadow. (3) The initial "Stop run" candle needs to appear 1-3 intervals after a WRB.

Yes, and we should keep in mind this is only one type of the many reversal patterns and possibilities at our areas of interest. We have 2 bar reversal, which is what was in that picture I posted, hangman(for short), inverted hammer(for long) as well as combinations of the above (I have rules being formulated for these as well). I also think whether the high probability zone in question is via a HG/WRB zone or a S&D zone must be taken into account. Low volume test reversals happen more in HG areas and high volume rejections happen at S&D zones. I think one important rule is if price confirms the reversal pattern and you're waiting for pullback, price shouldn't ever open and close above (or below) the stop run candle more than once (maybe not at all?). Also, since we are volume specialists, particular attention should be paid to the intervals after the stop run candle (and of course all of the candles really). Many times wicks to the upside on a shorting reversal trade (these wicks maybe being our pullback we're waiting for) can be low volume tests and/or inverted hammers on top (out of place), absorbing supply for a further push up. That's one place where the confirming entry pullback can get one in trouble. If the pullback was actually on low volume and the next candle closes up, its basically a failed test and price has a high probability of going up further and same for longs.

Another modification under review has to do with the confirmation candle. While it still needs to close below the body of the previous candle (for shorts), instead of having to close in its lower 33%, it only has to have a larger body than the previous interval.

I like this change also. I think I'm going to take the day off trading Friday and I can expand upon what I wrote here and add charts, and study more. I just wanted to get some thoughts down before I forgot what I was thinking: ) Long night and just got back from a show, I usually never stay up this late! Please feel free to correct my mistakes and tell me if I'm completely off base with this.

اصلاح اول برای من این است که سیگنال ورود تا وقتی حداقل یک tick/pip از الگو داخل یک Buying یا Selling Aggression Zone باشد یا روی آن، «معتبر» است.

قطعاً، آن‌ها یک عدد دلخواه دارند فقط برای اینکه قانونی داشته باشند. در واقع خیلی از قوانینشان همین‌طور است؛ کافی است قیمت وارد زون شود یا به آن بخورد.

اصلاح دیگر این است که کندل «Stop run» باید: نسبت به بازهٔ قبلی سقف بالاتر (برای فروش) یا کف پایین‌تر (برای خرید) بسازد. سایهٔ بالایی/پایینی کندل «Stop run» باید بزرگ‌تر از ترکیب بدنه و سایهٔ مقابل باشد. کندل «Stop run» اولیه باید 1-3 بازه بعد از یک WRB ظاهر شود.

بله، و باید به خاطر داشته باشیم که این فقط یکی از انواع الگوهای برگشت و احتمالاتِ بسیار در نواحی موردعلاقهٔ ماست. ما 2 bar reversal داریم که همان چیزی بود که در آن تصویر پست کردم، hangman (برای فروش)، inverted hammer (برای خرید) و همچنین ترکیب‌های موارد بالا (برای این‌ها هم دارم قوانین می‌نویسم). همچنین فکر می‌کنم باید در نظر گرفت که زون با احتمال بالا در سؤال، از نوع زون HG/WRB است یا زون S&D. برگشت‌های low volume test بیشتر در نواحی HG اتفاق می‌افتند و high volume rejection‌ها در زون‌های S&D. فکر می‌کنم یک قانون مهم این است که اگر قیمت الگوی برگشت را تأیید کرد و تو منتظر pullback هستی، قیمت هرگز نباید بیش از یک بار بالای (یا زیر) کندل stop run باز و بسته شود (شاید اصلاً؟). همچنین، چون ما متخصص حجم هستیم، باید توجه ویژه‌ای به بازه‌های بعد از کندل stop run داشت (و در واقع به همهٔ کندل‌ها). خیلی وقت‌ها فیتی‌های رو به بالا در یک معامله برگشتِ فروش (که شاید همان pullback‌هایی باشند که منتظرشان هستیم) می‌توانند low volume test و/یا inverted hammer‌های بی‌جای رویشان باشند که supply را برای یک فشار صعودی بیشتر جذب می‌کنند. این جایی است که pullbackِ confirmation entry می‌تواند آدم را به دردسر بیندازد. اگر pullback واقعاً روی حجم کم بود و کندل بعدی بالا بسته شود، اساساً یک تست شکست‌خورده است و احتمال زیادی دارد قیمت بیشتر بالا برود و برای خرید‌ها هم همین‌طور.

اصلاح دیگری که در حال بررسی است به کندل تأیید مربوط است. در حالی که هنوز باید زیر بدنهٔ کندل قبلی (برای فروش) بسته شود، به‌جای اینکه مجبور باشد در 33% پایینی آن بسته شود، فقط باید بدنه‌ای بزرگ‌تر از بازهٔ قبلی داشته باشد.

این تغییر را هم دوست دارم. فکر می‌کنم جمعه معامله را تعطیل می‌کنم تا بتوانم روی آنچه اینجا نوشتم بیشتر بسط دهم و چارت اضافه کنم و بیشتر مطالعه کنم. فقط می‌خواستم قبل از اینکه یادم برود چه فکر می‌کردم این ایده‌ها را بنویسم: ) شب طولانی بود و تازه از یک کنسرت برگشته‌ام، معمولاً این‌قدر دیر بیدار نمی‌مانم! لطفاً آزاد باش خطاهایم را تصحیح کنید و بگویید اگر کاملاً از مسیر خارج شدم.

There is so much to go over I'm not sure where to start. The DTFL confirming entry is actually an aggressive entry and that's why there are so many rules to go along with it, they don't worry about why price moves how it does, they kind of believe that it is rather futile to try and understand why. We know why price moves why it does, S&D. One thing on my mind is the retrace. It's not like one wants price to retrace against the reversal for any reason than for it to be a test for supply or demand and then for it to confirm in the direction of their trade the following candle. DTFL guys have no idea why price retraces (I've talked to Sterling about it), yet they take that retrace (they take it at 15 ticks at least usually 12 ticks from the high/low of stop run candle, it doesn't have to retrace into the wick for them). This is fine, it really gives one a great price to enter the trade. Like I said in the previous post, the following intervals just have to be monitored for failed tests and for price opening and closing above the level one is using. Another thing is the "stop run". For them, the stop run is because "SM" is searching for the liquidity to help them move price in the direction they want it to go (opposite of the stop run). We know price doesn't need a "stop run" to move in a direction. A stop run is a juicy bonus but it's not the reason price turns direction 30+ ticks. Supply sitting at an upper level is more of the reason price turns and goes down than stops being triggered at said level. We know every buyer is really a seller and vice versa which would help "SM" absorb their selling for instance if they ran prices up to actually desire for price to go down. Everyone who was short would become a buyer at that level, buying what "SM" was selling. This line of thinking gets rather convoluted though because said scenario should also trigger an up move according to other philosophies. What I'm getting at is there should be rules for non "stop run" reversals also, which happen a lot of the time. One example from today, I'll show the 3m and 1m chart, they both have examples of non stop run reversals at the same spot. Here is 3m overview chart: 3m

3m. 1. Enters an area that was previously a VHV WRW(wick) area of resistance and now support. 2. Price rejects on UHV, closing on the high but not above body of previous candle. This is alright, we just need it to close above the body of candle #1 within

number of

intervals (1 or 2?) 3. Closes above interval 1, also on its highs. 4. I realize this doesn't retrace into the wick, I'm not sure how I feel about retracing all the way into the wick. Retraces within 8 ticks of the low of interval 1 (I have no set number of ticks yet that it should retrace, DTFL uses 15, that's too much for me, I'm thinking 10 at least). This is where it can get messy. This retrace is also a LVT (lowest volume in prev 6 candles), that does confirm the next interval, even though that interval has a huge upper wick. Taking the trade at the bottom end of interval 4, would allow one to have a stop of 15 say, if the rule was 10 tick retrace at least (10 ticks to bottom of wick and 5 for cushion). One more thing about the LVT too, this last 2 weeks more than half my trades have been on them alone. That makes for some really easy rules. The stop run/2bar reversal/hangman or whatever, can end up doing whatever it does at the area of interest. We don't care because we don't enter until we see a LVT that confirms, within number of candles. That's Sebastian Manby style entry. You miss out on ticks, but are able to have a stop loss of 1-5 ticks at most. Just another idea I suppose.

Now for the 1m and the inverted hammer type entry. This is the same entry spot as 3m. For me the Inverted hammer at an area such as this offers the best risk to reward. One can have a very small stop because if price goes lower it is really then a test (for demand here) on high or low volume, that has passed. The only other reason would be a stop run candle like a hammer after it. A hammer > inverted hammer is a better setup. 1. Inverted hammer on UUHV, right at the demand zone in blue. The interval before it is basically a hammer type stop run as well on UHV with UUHV IH as result. 2. Confirms up above IH. 3. A LVT 4. LVT confirmation candle. For me on an IH type entry its just long after price crosses IH body with 2-5 tick stop in case price goes a bit below again. Waiting for the LVT here still gives a great entry.

HiddenGap wrote: The rules:

1. There may be a variation that does not include a WRB, but as of this time the first requirement is the appearance of a WRB What makes you need a WRB within 3 candles? I've noticed a lot of times its a good sign of reversal when there is a WRB say going up, and then contracting volatility for a good amount of bars slowly going up into a stop run candle at an area of interest.

2. After the appearance of a WRB, we need to see the "Stop run" candle(#1) within 1-3 intervals. Rather than thinking of this interval as a "Stop run" candle, it may be more appropriate to think of it as Supply Swamping Demand (SSD) for shorts or Demand Swamping Supply (DSS) for longs. In the case of SSD, the candle's upper shadow must be greater than the combination of the body and the lower shadow. The SSD candle must also make a higher high than the previous candle.

SSD and DSS is a great way of thinking of it, especially if other candle patterns are used instead of just stop run, big wick candle.

3. The confirmation candle must close lower than the body of the previous candle (for shorts) and higher than the body of the previous candle for longs. The other requirement is that the body of the confirmation candle is larger than the body of the previous candle.

I like this, I also like the progression of candles type of outlook. Say the confirmation candle doesn't completely confirm, as long as the next one finally closes below/above it etc.

4. After the confirmation candle (#2), price must retrace to within the range of the upper shadow (for short) within 3 intervals. Excluding the WRB, this is a minimum 3 interval pattern and a maximum 5 interval pattern.

That's what we have so far............

Just a few ideas, I have a lot more to write about this. I hope this isn't too disjointed. The girlfriend is making me do more normal human things so got to go for awhile: )

چیزهای زیادی برای مرور هست، مطمئن نیستم از کجا شروع کنم. DTFL confirming entry در واقع یک ورود تهاجمی است و به همین دلیل قوانین زیادی همراهش است؛ آن‌ها نگران نیستند قیمت چرا این‌طور حرکت می‌کند، نوعی باور دارند که تلاش برای فهمیدن چرا، نسبتاً بیهوده است. ما می‌دانیم قیمت چرا این‌طور حرکت می‌کند: S&D. یک چیز که ذهنم را مشغول کرده retrace است. مسئله این نیست که کسی بخواهد قیمت را به‌خاطر هر دلیلی خلاف برگشت ببرد؛ مسئله این است که retrace یک تست برای supply یا demand باشد و بعد کندل بعدی در جهت تریدشان تأیید کند. بچه‌های DTFL نمی‌دانند قیمت چرا retrace می‌کند (با Sterling درباره‌اش حرف زده‌ام)، با این حال آن retrace را می‌گیرند (آن را حداقل در 15 tick، معمولاً 12 tick از سقف/کف کندل stop run می‌گیرند؛ برای آن‌ها لازم نیست تا فیتی برگردد). این خوب است، واقعاً قیمتی عالی برای ورود به معامله می‌دهد. همان‌طور که در پست قبلی گفتم، بازه‌های بعدی فقط باید برای تست‌های شکست‌خورده و برای باز و بسته شدن قیمت بالای سطح مورداستفاده مانیتور شوند. چیز دیگر «stop run» است. برای آن‌ها، stop run این است که «SM» دنبال liquidity است تا به آن‌ها کمک کند قیمت را در جهت دلخواهشان حرکت دهند (برعکس stop run). ما می‌دانیم قیمت برای حرکت در یک جهت به «stop run» نیاز ندارد؛ stop run یک بونوس پرچرب است اما دلیل این نیست که قیمت 30+ tick جهت عوض کند. supply‌ای که در سطح بالاتری نشسته بیشتر از فعال‌شدن استاپ‌ها در آن سطح دلیل برگشت و افت قیمت است. ما می‌دانیم هر خریدار در واقع فروشنده است و برعکس، که به «SM» مثلاً کمک می‌کند اگر قیمت‌ها را بالا ببرند و در واقع بخواهند قیمت پایین برود، فروششان را جذب کند. همه‌ای که فروش بودند در آن سطح خریدار می‌شدند و چیزی را که «SM» می‌فروخت می‌خریدند. این خط فکری کمی پیچیده می‌شود چون همان سناریو طبق فلسفه‌های دیگر هم باید یک حرکت صعودی را تریگر کند. منظوری که دارم این است که باید برای برگشت‌های غیر «stop run» هم قوانین باشد، که خیلی وقت‌ها اتفاق می‌افتند. یک مثال از امروز، چارت 3m و 1m را نشان می‌دهم که هر دو در همان نقطه مثال‌هایی از برگشت‌های غیر stop run دارند. این چارت کلی 3m است:

3m. 1. وارد ناحیه‌ای می‌شود که قبلاً ناحیهٔ resistance از نوع VHV WRW(wick) بود و حالا support است. 2. قیمت روی UHV رد می‌شود، روی سقف می‌بندد اما بالای بدنهٔ کندل قبلی نه. این اشکالی ندارد، فقط باید درون

تعداد

بازه (1 یا 2؟) بالای بدنهٔ کندل #1 بسته شود. 3. بالای بازهٔ 1 بسته می‌شود، باز هم روی سقف‌هایش. 4. متوجه می‌شم که این به فیتی برنمی‌گردد، مطمئن نیستم دربارهٔ برگشتن کامل تا فیتی چه فکری دارم. تا 8 tick از کف بازهٔ 1 برمی‌گردد (هنوز تعداد tick مشخصی برای برگردد ندارد، DTFL از 15 استفاده می‌کند که برای من زیاد است، حداقل 10 فکر می‌کنم). اینجاست که می‌تواند به‌هم‌ریخته شود. این retrace همچنین یک LVT است (کمترین حجم در 6 کندل قبلی) که بازهٔ بعدی را تأیید می‌کند، هرچند آن بازه فیتی بالایی بزرگ دارد. گرفتن معامله در انتهای پایین بازهٔ 4، به کسی اجازه می‌دهد استاپی مثلاً 15 داشته باشد، اگر قانون حداقل 10 tick retrace باشد (10 tick تا ته فیتی و 5 برای حاشیه). یک چیز دیگر دربارهٔ LVT هم هست: این 2 هفتهٔ اخیر بیش از نیمی از تریدهایم فقط روی همین‌ها بوده. این قوانین واقعاً آسانی می‌سازد. stop run/2bar reversal/hangman یا هرچه، می‌تواند در ناحیهٔ موردعلاقه هر کاری بکند؛ مهم نیست چون وارد نمی‌شویم تا LVT‌ی که تأیید می‌کند را ببینیم، ظرف تعداد کندل مشخص. این همان سبک ورود Sebastian Manby است؛ چند tick از دست می‌دهی، اما می‌توانی حد ضرر حداکثر 1-5 tick داشته باشی. فقط ایدهٔ دیگری است به نظرم.

حالا برای 1m و ورود از نوع inverted hammer. این همان نقطهٔ ورود 3m است. برای من Inverted hammer در ناحیه‌ای مثل این بهترین risk-to-reward را می‌دهد. می‌توان استاپ خیلی کوچکی داشت چون اگر قیمت پایین‌تر برود، واقعاً یک تست (برای demand اینجا) روی حجم بالا یا پایین است که رد شده. تنها دلیل دیگر، کندل stop run مثل hammer بعد از آن است. hammer inverted hammer ستاپ بهتری است. 1. Inverted hammer روی UUHV، دقیقاً روی زون demand آبی. بازهٔ قبل از آن اساساً یک stop run از نوع hammer روی UHV است با نتیجهٔ UUHV IH. 2. بالای IH تأیید می‌کند. 3. یک LVT 4. کندل تأیید LVT. برای من در ورود از نوع IH فقط بعد از عبور قیمت از بدنهٔ IH خرید می‌کنم با استاپ 2-5 tick برای حالتی که قیمت دوباره کمی پایین برود. صبر برای LVT اینجا هنوز ورود عالی می‌دهد.

HiddenGap نوشت: قوانین:

1. ممکن است گونه‌ای وجود داشته باشد که WRB نداشته باشد، اما تا این زمان اولین شرط، ظاهر شدن WRB است چه چیزی باعث می‌شود WRB را ظرف 3 کندل لازم داشته باشی؟ متوجه شدم خیلی وقت‌ها وقتی WRB‌ی مثلاً صعودی هست و بعد نوسان برای تعداد خوبی از بارها جمع می‌شود و آرام‌آرام به سمت یک کندل stop run در ناحیهٔ موردعلاقه می‌رود، نشانهٔ خوبی از برگشت است.

2. بعد از ظاهر شدن WRB، باید کندل «Stop run»(#1) را ظرف 1-3 بازه ببینیم. به‌جای فکر کردن به این بازه به‌عنوان کندل «Stop run»، شاید مناسب‌تر باشد آن را Supply Swamping Demand (SSD) برای فروش یا Demand Swamping Supply (DSS) برای خرید بدانیم. در مورد SSD، سایهٔ بالایی کندل باید بزرگ‌تر از ترکیب بدنه و سایهٔ پایینی باشد. کندل SSD همچنین باید سقف بالاتری از کندل قبلی بسازد.

SSD و DSS راه فوق‌العاده‌ای برای فکر کردن به آن است، مخصوصاً اگر به‌جای فقط stop run یا کندل فیتی بزرگ از الگوهای کندل دیگر هم استفاده شود.

3. کندل تأیید باید برای فروش پایین‌تر از بدنهٔ کندل قبلی و برای خرید بالاتر از بدنهٔ کندل قبلی بسته شود. شرط دیگر این است که بدنهٔ کندل تأیید بزرگ‌تر از بدنهٔ کندل قبلی باشد.

این را دوست دارم، چشم‌انداز پیشرفت نوع کندل‌ها را هم دوست دارم. فرض کن کندل تأیید کاملاً تأیید نکند، تا وقتی کندل بعدی بالاخره زیر/بالای آن بسته شود و غیره.

4. بعد از کندل تأیید (#2)، قیمت باید ظرف 3 بازه به داخل رنج سایهٔ بالایی (برای فروش) برگردد. بدون در نظر گرفتن WRB، این حداقل الگوی 3 بازه‌ای و حداکثر الگوی 5 بازه‌ای است.

این است آنچه تا اینجا داریم…

فقط چند ایده است، چیزهای بیشتری دربارهٔ این برای نوشتن دارم. امیدوارم خیلی ناهماهنگ نباشد. نامزد/دوستم داره کارهای انسانی عادی‌تری بهم می‌ده پس باید کمی بروم: )

posts.t: A bit more food for thought. One other idea of the confirming entry I'm not sure if you want to add or dismiss. A lot of times a candle is so big that for the next candle to close below it, it would be so far back for a pullback as to rarely happen, or not be a good thing. So, as long as candle 2 closes on its lows, and the next candle closes below number 2, it may be a confirmed trade (depending on if you go by body closing below previous candle and in lower 1/3 or body size), ready for a pullback or instant taking of trade if within stop loss limits. This 3m chart has the general idea, the area of reversal may or may not really be an area of interest but for this purpose lets say it is. I also would never have taken this specific trade but it shows the general idea, in a real market at least, instead of drawing the idea out in paint or something. 1. WRB enters supply zone (already I'm not sure if you said the WRB candle can be the stop run or initiating candle or not?) 2. Closes on it's lows, below close of interval 1. It doesn't close below the previous interval so we must have the next interval close below number 2. You can add rules here for how many intervals are allowed for this cycle to complete, 1 or 2 seems fine. 3. Closes below number 2 (if you go by body size this can't confirm because the body is smaller, if you go by percentage of close in lower 1/3, then it confirms). 4. hieronymus wrote:...One thing on my mind is the retrace. It's not like one wants price to retrace against the reversal for any reason than for it to be a test for supply or demand and then for it to confirm in the direction of their trade the following candle. DTFL guys have no idea why price retraces (I've talked to Sterling about it), yet they take that retrace (they take it at 15 ticks at least usually 12 ticks from the high/low of stop run candle, it doesn't have to retrace into the wick for them). This is fine, it really gives one a great price to enter the trade.

It doesn't really matter "why" price retraces. What matters is the concept. They place a stop 5 pips above/below the high/low of the "Stop run" candle. They also never want to risk more than 20 pips. Often times after the confirmation candle, you need price to pull back so as to stay within the preset risk parameter.

From our perspective, a retrace back into the Upper/Lower shadow serves two purposes. 1) it will allow one to minimize risk. 2) Since the Long Upper/Lower shadow represents a temporary shift in the Supply/Demand dynamic in the market, we would be entering within the area of that shift.

hieronymus wrote:...Another thing is the "stop run". For them, the stop run is because "SM" is searching for the liquidity to help them move price in the direction they want it to go (opposite of the stop run). We know price doesn't need a "stop run" to move in a direction. A stop run is a juicy bonus but it's not the reason price turns direction 30+ ticks. Supply sitting at an upper level is more of the reason price turns and goes down than stops being triggered at said level.

Things are a little different from our perspective. Rather than calling it a "Stop Run" candle, I have suggested "Demand Swamping Supply (DSS) or Supply Swamping Demand (SSD)". However, I think we can simply use the term "Start Point" candle.

hieronymus wrote:..We know every buyer is really a seller and vice versa which would help "SM" absorb their selling for instance if they ran prices up to actually desire for price to go down. Everyone who was short would become a buyer at that level, buying what "SM" was selling. This line of thinking gets rather convoluted though because said scenario should also trigger an up move according to other philosophies.

There are a few absolute truths about the market. One is as soon as you buy, you become a seller. And as soon as you sell, you become a buyer. Another truth is that the market moves more because of traders trying to exit losing positions, than it does because of traders entering new ones.

posts.t:
Here's an example of the flexibility this entry "pattern" can allow. What I want to create is a rule based entry that is specific in nature, yet general enough to allow for a wide range of possibilities.

We begin with the appearance of a WRB. There are a couple of ways to do this. We wait for the appearance of the WRB and then focus on the next 1-3 intervals for our Start Point Candle. Or, we can identify the Start Point Candle first, and look back 1-3 intervals to see if there is a WRB

I think it is easier to identify the WRB and see it as an alert that a signal might be coming.

1': This is our Start Point. It is making a higher high than the previous candle and its upper shadow is greater than the combination of its lower shadow and its body.

2': This candle does not confirm. It does not close lower than the body of the previous candle (the Start Point Candle) and its body is not large than the body of the previous candle.

At this point there is no trade signal.

But wait.

The next candle makes a higher high than the previous candle and has an upper shadow greater than the combination of its lower shadow and body. And it is within 1-3 intervals of the WRB. We have a valid Start Point Candle. A new #1.

: This candle does close lower than the body of the Start Point Candle and also has a body greater than the body of the Start Point Candle.

: We can look to enter as price retraces into the area of the Upper Shadow of our Start Point Candle.

So this is a "Valid" signal, but it does not appear in a Zone. Therefore, no trade would be taken,

اینجا مثالی از انعطافی که این «الگوی» ورود می‌تواند بدهد. چیزی که می‌خواهم بسازم ورودی مبتنی بر قانون است که ذاتاً دقیق است، اما به‌اندازهٔ کافی کلی تا طیف وسیعی از احتمالات را بپذیرد.

با ظاهر شدن WRB شروع می‌کنیم. چند راه برای این کار هست: یا منتظر ظاهر شدن WRB می‌مانیم و بعد روی 1-3 بازهٔ بعدی برای Start Point Candle تمرکز می‌کنیم؛ یا اول Start Point Candle را مشخص می‌کنیم و 1-3 بازه به عقب نگاه می‌کنیم ببینیم WRB هست یا نه.

فکر می‌کنم تشخیص WRB و دیدنش به‌عنوان هشداری که شاید سیگنالی در راه است، آسان‌تر است.

1': این Start Point ماست. نسبت به کندل قبلی سقف بالاتری می‌سازد و سایهٔ بالایی‌اش بزرگ‌تر از ترکیب سایهٔ پایینی و بدنه‌اش است.

2': این کندل تأیید نمی‌کند؛ زیر بدنهٔ کندل قبلی (Start Point Candle) نمی‌بندد و بدنه‌اش هم از بدنهٔ کندل قبلی بزرگ‌تر نیست.

در این نقطه سیگنال تریدی نیست.

اما صبر کن.

کندل بعدی نسبت به کندل قبلی سقف بالاتری می‌سازد و سایهٔ بالایی‌اش بزرگ‌تر از ترکیب سایهٔ پایینی و بدنه‌اش است و در 1-3 بازهٔ WRB است. Start Point Candle معتبری داریم؛ یک #1 جدید.

این کندل زیر بدنهٔ Start Point Candle می‌بندد و بدنه‌ای بزرگ‌تر از بدنهٔ Start Point Candle دارد.

می‌توانیم با برگردیدن قیمت به داخل ناحیهٔ سایهٔ بالایی Start Point Candle دنبال ورود باشیم.

پس این یک سیگنال «معتبر» است، اما در زونی ظاهر نمی‌شود؛ پس هیچ تریدی گرفته نمی‌شد،
